Separate depth from undertone

Skin depth describes how light or deep your complexion appears. Undertone describes the warmer, cooler or more neutral cast underneath. These are different features, so people with a similar complexion can prefer different lipstick colours. Looking at several shades on your lips is more useful than applying a strict rule based on one feature.

Compare warmer and cooler shades

Peach, terracotta and warmer brown shades may create a harmonious look on a warm complexion. Rosy, berry and cooler pink shades can suit a cooler colour preference. Neutral undertones give you room to compare both groups. A contrasting shade can also be an intentional style choice; the aim is a colour you enjoy wearing.

Account for natural lip colour

A sheer tint allows more of your natural lip colour to show, while a more opaque lipstick gives stronger definition. A nude that looks pale in a hand swatch may appear quite different on pigmented lips. Compare the depth of the lipstick with your lips as well as your complexion, and try a lip liner if you want a more defined edge.

Test the whole look

Check the shade beside your blush, clothing and eye makeup. Daylight helps you see the colour without the strong cast of some indoor lights. Start with one layer, then adjust the intensity. Step 5: tidy, refresh and remove gently

Use a clean cotton bud with a little suitable remover to correct an edge if needed. After meals, tidy worn areas before refreshing the colour instead of coating over several old layers.
